article.headline: Veo 3 Fast Undercuts a Rival That Lacks Audio
article.lede: Google's Veo 3 Fast costs $0.20 per eight-second clip — complete with native audio and dialogue — while MiniMax's Hailuo 02 runs $0.25 for a six-second, 768p clip that ships without any sound. The comparison, circulated by AI developer @maxescu, inverts the usual expectation that bundled audio commands a premium. For anyone building video pipelines at scale, the gap is real money.
article.body:
The *text-to-video* market — where a model converts a written prompt directly into a short video clip — has become crowded enough that pricing, not raw quality, is increasingly the differentiator. Veo 3 Fast is a throughput-optimised tier of Google's third-generation model, available through the Flow platform; it trades some fidelity headroom against speed and cost. Hailuo 02 is MiniMax's second-generation model, developed by the Shanghai-based AI startup of the same name and notable for *image-to-video* animation and end-frame control.

On the numbers the tweet presents, Veo 3 Fast wins on every dimension that scales with usage. It is cheaper per clip ($0.20 vs. $0.25), delivers longer output (eight seconds versus six), and generates **native audio and dialogue** — a capability Hailuo 02 lacks entirely. Hailuo 02 edges ahead only on resolution (768p vs. 720p), a difference rarely perceptible at web output sizes.

Hailuo 02 does have genuine strengths the cost table obscures. According to the Artificial Analysis Video Arena Leaderboard, it ranks second among video models with a benchmark score that outpaces Veo 3, suggesting its motion consistency and prompt fidelity are strong even without audio. Its end-frame image control — letting a creator specify both the first and last frame of a clip — is a production feature Veo 3 Fast does not offer, making it a better fit for composited narrative work.

The comparison is specifically between Veo 3 **Fast** and Hailuo 02, not between Google's premium Veo 3.1 tier (which costs roughly 400 credits per generation, versus Hailuo 02's 70). That distinction matters: the full Veo 3.1 supports 4K resolution and reference-image input but is dramatically more expensive. Developers optimising for cost should treat Fast and 3.1 as separate products with separate use cases.

The broader implication is that **native audio generation** — long considered a high-cost add-on — is being commoditised into base-tier pricing. If Google holds the Veo 3 Fast price point, rivals without audio pipelines will face pressure to build or license one, or compete on the narrower ground of image animation and frame control.

concepts.definition: A class of AI models that accepts a written prompt and produces a short video clip. The model learns statistical patterns across large video datasets to synthesise motion, lighting, and — in newer systems — synchronised audio without any human editing.

A mode in which the AI takes a still image as its starting frame and generates realistic motion outward from it. Unlike pure text-to-video, the model is anchored to a specific visual composition, making it useful for animating illustrations, product shots, or portraits.

When a video model produces sound — effects, ambient noise, or spoken dialogue — in the same forward pass that generates the image frames. This differs from layering a separate text-to-speech or audio model onto a silent clip in post-production, which adds latency and cost.

A feature that lets the user supply both a starting image and an ending image, with the model filling in the motion between them. This gives creators predictable compositional control across a clip rather than accepting wherever the model decides to end.

article.fact_check: The tweet states Hailuo 02 produces 6-second clips at the $0.25 price point. Research sources indicate Hailuo 02 supports clips up to 10 seconds, suggesting the 6-second figure may reflect a specific credit-pack tier or default setting rather than a hard model cap. Readers building cost models should verify the exact duration available at the cited credit price on Hailuo's platform. Additionally, the comparison is specifically against Veo 3 Fast — a cheaper, faster tier — not Google's premium Veo 3.1, which costs substantially more and supports 4K output.

ticker_googl.name: Alphabet Inc. (Class A)
ticker_googl.blurb: Alphabet is the parent company of Google, the world's dominant search engine, as well as YouTube, the Google Cloud Platform, and a portfolio of moonshot bets (Waymo, DeepMind, Verily). Search advertising accounts for the majority of revenue, but the cloud division has grown into a multi-billion-dollar profit centre. Alphabet is also a leading player in generative AI, having developed the Gemini family of large language models and integrated them across its product suite.
ticker_googl.recent: Alphabet reported FY2025 revenue of approximately $370 billion, with Google Cloud crossing $50 billion annually. The company has faced antitrust scrutiny in both the US and EU, with a US federal court ruling in 2024 that Google holds an illegal monopoly in general search. Despite regulatory headwinds, the stock has benefited from AI-driven search enhancements and strong cloud growth. Paul Pelosi exercised call options with a $150 strike (purchased January 2025, exercised January 2026) gaining approximately 75% over the period.
